https://github.com/thunderbird/thunderbird-android/issues/9981 https://github.com/thunderbird/thunderbird-android/issues/6197

Synchronisation

For timely synchronisation, please check the app is excluded from any battery optimisation and allowed to run in the background. This is enabled using android settings. Navigate to android settings > all apps > Thunderbird > Battery Usage

Sync is managed on a per folder basis and only enabled by default for Inbox. To toggle sync on for other folders.

1. Open the account sidebar with your account folders displayed 2. Press the manage folders button (bottom of list) 3. Tap a folder name 4. Tap "Enable Sync"

You also have the choice to enable the PUSH feature (Imap idle) which delivers emails immediately. Guide: https://support.mozilla.org/en-US/kb/configure-push-email-thunderbird-android

RBLevin said
Unified Folders don't unify.

To display the content of a folder within Unified inbox, toggle the "Unify" setting to ON.

TB have an open pull request to add unified Outbox, Drafts, Sent, Archive, Spam and Trash folders in a future update. see PR #11744

You can find more information about active and planned development on the below roadmap. https://roadmaps.thunderbird.net/en-US/android/

Feel free to share your ideas and improvement suggestions on Mozilla connect. https://connect.mozilla.org/t5/ideas/idb-p/ideas/label-name/thunderbird%20android

content:
Hi John

I can replicate your behaviour and think i can explain what's happening.

After you cleared the local messages and change the local folder size, your next step was pressing the load 100 more button. There's no mention of you synchronising the folder with the server before pressing the button.

When I replicate your steps I observe double the qty of messages downloaded compared to the local folder size value.

I believe pressing load more is doing 2 actions after local messages are cleared. 1. Performs an initial folder sync, downloads the first batch of emails (100). 2. Downloads the second batch of emails (100 more) requested because the load more button was pressed.

Can you try these steps instead. 1. Change the local folder size to your desired value (100) ++. 2. Change to a different folder, then switch back to inbox again. 3. Clear the local messages for inbox 4. Perform a pull down swipe gesture to sync the folder (loads first batch 100 emails) 5. Press the load 100 more button (only if you need an additional 100 emails).

++ I noticed the currently selected folder doesn't immediately pick up setting changes to local folder size until a different folder or account has been selected. The load x more messages button displays and uses the old values until after a change, hence step 2.

Unify

Toggling the Unify folder setting tells the app to display said folders content within the Unified Inbox. After electing to Unify sent and draft folders, it's the expected app behaviour to display their content within the Unified Inbox. Actions such as delete, move etc are performed on the original email.

The app doesn't yet have separate Unified Outbox, sent, draft, trash or Archive folders. That is a planned feature addition likely to arrive in a future update. See below for more info. https://github.com/thunderbird/thunderbird-android/pull/11744

Please see the guide linked below that explains how to import your email account details from Thunderbird desktop to the android app. The desktop app will generate a QR code that you scan using the mobile app.

https://support.mozilla.org/en-US/kb/thunderbird-android-import#w_how-to-import-from-thunderbird-desktop

This will usually import your email address, password and server configuration.

If your account is using oAuth 2.0 authentication rather than normal password, you may still need to complete your account providers sign-in steps within the mobile app.

A quick way to get your email address in Thunderbird desktop:

  • Click Write to compose a new email.
  • Look at the From field. Your email address should appear there.

If Thunderbird desktop uses password authentication to connect to your email providers server, you should find it stored in the password manager.

See the below guide. https://support.mozilla.org/en-US/kb/password-manager-remember-delete-change-tb

Thunderbird doesn't store your email account password when oauth 2.0 authentication is being used.

content:
Have you tried importing your account setting from desktop to mobile using the QR code method. This transfers your account password and server configuration. See the guide below.

https://support.mozilla.org/en-US/kb/thunderbird-android-import#w_how-to-import-from-thunderbird-desktop

Password

Is the long password 16 characters in length. If so, it may be an "app password". An app password can be used to setup an account in Thunderbird Android.

Most email providers no longer allow email clients to authenticate using an account holders normal password. They prefer more modern secure authentication such as oAuth.

As a less secure alternative, they allow users to generate a 16 character "App password" using their web-mail settings page. This is entered in the email client instead of a users normal account password.

You can read more about app passwords in the link below.

https://www.historytools.org/docs/what-is-an-app-password-and-when-do-you-need-one-instead-of-your-normal-sign-in

If you require but don't remember your normal account password, most email providers have a password reset button on their webmail sign-in page.

There is an open github issue report for the error message you observe. "SmtpClientAuthentication is disabled for the mailbox"

https://github.com/thunderbird/thunderbird-android/issues/10787

We are really sorry you all are facing this issue. Microsoft has been making significant changes recently without providing any disclosure or documentation that could help us understand these changes or how to address them. It becomes even more challenging when we don't know the specific configuration settings your account has, as we need to replicate those settings in order to troubleshoot and resolve the issue. If anyone is capable of coding and is also facing this issue, we would be really glad to receive any assistance with the investigation. Any help fixing this issue is really appreciated. Thanks for your understanding

There's currently no fix or workaround.

Your case seems unusual in that it was working for you a few weeks ago, but has now ceased. It's possible Microsoft has applied a policy change on your account which blocks the way TB connects, inline with other outlook.com accounts.

Office365 Corporate/University/School accounts are different as IT administrators have the controls to enable/disable SMTP Authentication. These controls are not offered to users of personal outlook accounts.
